notes: GGUF-first; CUDA/HIP/Vulkan/Metal/SYCL are separate build/device profiles; OpenVINO is in-progress; only Hexagon NPU is experimental and Windows instructions require test signing; generic structured/tool/multimodal support is model/template-specific. Covert adapter is currently recovery-only, uncomposed and feature-limited.

Linux working runtime; native Windows unsupported; CUDA prebuilt CC>=7.5; ROCm and Intel XPU are tightly scoped Linux profiles; Apple path is a separate vLLM-Metal plugin; GGUF external plugin is experimental. Supports broad HF formats/quantization, but not an ordinary Windows local fallback.

Optimized high-throughput/agentic serving; AMD GPU documentation focuses on specific Instinct families, not all Radeon; XPU and Apple paths have separate constraints. Not justified as first workstation adapter. GGUF loader is documented, but quantization compatibility varies by backend (CUDA/Ascend listed; AMD not listed); not GGUF parity.

Apple Silicon + Metal; supports streaming and a local OpenAI-shaped server; model input/quantization paths are MLX/HF-specific. Separate MLX package identity. Tool behavior depends on model/template/server formatter; not a cross-platform adapter.

Intel CPU/GPU/NPU-focused; OS/backend support depends on OpenVINO Runtime device plugins. LLM models typically export to OpenVINO IR; NPU needs constrained symmetric INT4 path. GGUF is preview/limited. GenAI library is not inherently an OpenAI server.

Upstream matrix lists CPU/CUDA/DirectML/OpenVINO/QNN/WebGPU and AMD GPU under development. QNN is explicit on Windows ARM64/Linux ARM64 but requires an ONNX GenAI package with compiled QNN graph artifacts. Core API is not an HTTP server and generic ONNX is not sufficient.

NVIDIA CUDA-specific compiled/runtime stack; treat engine plans as hardware/runtime-bound derived artifacts. Apache project license does not establish that all vendor libraries are redistributable. Performance specialty, not universal backend.

Broad CUDA/HIP/Vulkan/Metal/mobile/WebGPU matrix but requires MLC weight conversion and often target-specific compilation. WSL Vulkan is explicitly work in progress. API availability does not prove Covert lifecycle/governance.

runtime_type: backend orchestrator/reference rather than one inference engine
notes: Useful comparison for backend variants/gallery, hardware-aware packaging and explicit model config. Capability cells are PARTIAL because they depend on selected backend; do not read as one runtime feature set. Covert should reuse design lessons, not depend on this orchestrator.

Strong Android/iOS/embedded delegate reach; LLM runner and OpenAI-shaped server are explicitly experimental/narrow. Models export to .pte; conversion and delegate builds create derived identities. Mobile/edge watch, not Windows ARM workstation answer.

MNN-LLM is a C++ engine with CPU/CUDA/Vulkan/Metal/OpenCL families and mobile/IoT reach; QNN and a newer Android Hexagon path require target-specific exported MNN/QNN packages. Official guide describes PyTorch/safetensors/GGUF conversion to MNN. No OpenAI-compatible server/governance path was established.

Current KT-Kernel path is Linux x86-64 and MoE-oriented: AVX2/AVX-512/AMX CPU plus NVIDIA SM80+ CUDA; older project docs describe AMD/Arc/Ascend-specific paths. Current serving examples integrate through SGLang and GGUF CPU weights. Specialized large-MoE path, not broad general model runtime.
